# dpdk-bind

This module is intended to be imported to set some interfaces in DPDK mode. Technically, that only means
binding NICs to the UIO driver.

Set the `igb_uio` tag to use igb_uio instead of uio_pci_generic.

Suggested usage example in your test:
```bash
%import@client dpdk-bind NIC=0
```

That will bind NIC 0 of the client node to uio_pci_generic and ensure pages are mounted.

Source: [`modules/dpdk-bind.npf`](https://github.com/tbarbette/npf/blob/main/modules/dpdk-bind.npf)

## Variables

| Variable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `NIC` | `0` | NIC index to bind |
| `DRIVER` | `uio_pci_generic`<br>`igb_uio` with `igb_uio` | Kernel driver to bind the NIC to, use the igb_uio tag rather than changing it |
